analysis.title: Weekly Investor Research: AI concerns drive further tech downside as US midterms loom
key_insights: The AI-hardware sell-off continued. The Philadelphia Semiconductor index (SOX) dropped 8.2% on Friday alone and is 27% below its June highs (-15% in October). It closed below its 200-day moving average for the first time since April 2025.

The 10-year UST yield is back at 4.9%, the first time since September, after round-tripping to over 5.3% in early October. Ashmore attributes this to de-leveraging and positioning dynamics plus some markdown in bond investors' expectations of AI capex driving nominal growth.

Ashmore sees little fundamental reason behind the sell-off so far. Tech derated with rising rates since June, and the September FOMC hike set the tone for another leg down, with tightening financing conditions hitting neoclouds and leveraged AI names first.
Pain has broadened to companies tied to large AI capex, including those with large net cash positions. Healthcare and consumer staples, classic risk-off rotation plays, each rose over 11% in October.

Relative to the S&P 500, US IT valuation fell from about 1.5x to 1.0x (12-month forward P/E from 32x to 18x) since July 2024. A 33% relative derating over about 26 months compares with the dotcom bust's roughly 40% decline from 2.3x to 1.4x. At 18x forward earnings, S&P IT is cheaper than at any point in the dotcom bust, where it bottomed at 19x in 2002.
EM IT stocks at 8.5x earnings are close to the cheapest levels of the 2000s so far.

Hyperscaler capex came in slightly softer than expected for Q3 2026, which Ashmore attributes to supply bottlenecks rather than oversupply. Hyperscaler outlooks point to capex rising significantly in USD terms in 2027.
Cloud revenue growth is rising each quarter, at 103% yoy at Google, 48% at Microsoft and 39% at Amazon. Ashmore says it is hard to believe we are near the end of the AI investment cycle.
Hedge fund de-leveraging likely amplified the moves in high-beta tech. Ashmore advises caution in the short term, with volatility likely to stay elevated.

US midterms this week are a risk event. Prediction markets price a 73% chance the Democrats take the Senate and 95% the House, which Ashmore says could add negative AI sentiment given Democrats' anti-data-centre rhetoric. Other models that adjust for poll biases suggest Republicans may keep the Senate.

Ashmore says the market perceives Middle East escalation risk rising after the midterms. A deal with Iran remains the main catalyst for a switch back to risk-on. Axios reported Netanyahu pressed Trump to strike Iran right after the midterms, while Trump prefers to let negotiations run and Bessent urges more time for economic pressure.

The Fed held rates on 28 October in a 10-2 vote, with Cook and Hammack wanting a hike. Markets price a 75% probability of a December hike. Chair Warsh reiterated commitment to returning inflation to target.

SK Hynix reported record Q3 operating profit of KRW 83.3trn, up 557% yoy, with operating margin above 80%. It said virtually all DRAM and HBM capacity through 2029 is covered by long-term agreements, and shares rebounded more than 10%.
Samsung Electronics confirmed Q3 operating profit of KRW 107.4trn, with chips 99% of the total and 2027 HBM capacity sold out, but net profit of KRW 75.1trn missed consensus and shares fell.

Brazilian assets slumped after Lula won a fourth term with 51.8% in a runoff. The BRL fell about 10% to 5.60/USD, the Ibovespa triggered a circuit breaker, and Brazilian stocks fell nearly 25% in USD terms on the week. MSCI Latam fell 15.3% over 5 days.

Fitch said Lula's re-election adds fiscal uncertainty, could limit Selic easing, and a failure to improve fiscal credibility could lead to a downgrade from BB. The Liberal Party holds the largest caucus in both houses, so the finance minister choice is a key signal.

Brent fell 6.3% on the week on evidence of progress in negotiations. Saudi Aramco raised Red Sea export capacity to about 8.2m bpd from 5m bpd pre-war, and ADNOC is fast-tracking a pipeline to roughly double export capacity outside Hormuz to about 3.6m bpd.

Argentina and IMF staff reached agreement on the third EFF review, which would unlock about USD 900m once approved by the board in early December. Net reserve accumulation beat the end-June target by about USD 4bn.

Egypt raised key rates by 100bps in a surprise move, its first hike since 2024, to a 20.0% deposit rate and 21.0% lending rate, citing inflation, risk-off sentiment and resumed portfolio outflows as the pound hit record lows.

Zelenskyy said Ukraine is ready to discuss territorial issues with Russia at leaders' level, an apparent shift under US pressure. Russia is ready to resume talks with the US and Ukraine after 4 November, possibly in Abu Dhabi.
The UST curve bull steepened, with two-year yields down 13bps on the week to 4.59%. US stocks fell 0.6%, led by semiconductors.
South Korea Q3 GDP rose 1.0% qoq against a 0.8% survey, driven by chip exports and equipment investment. Taiwan Q3 GDP rose 14.4% yoy against a 12.0% survey.

Samsung Electronics Q3 net profit of KRW 75.1trn missed consensus and shares fell, despite operating profit of KRW 107.4trn and 2027 HBM capacity sold out.

Middle East escalation after the midterms, with Iran threatening oil and gas facilities in five Gulf states if struck.

Financing concerns for leveraged AI names and hedge fund de-leveraging in high-beta tech.
Brazil fiscal credibility under Lula, with Fitch warning of a possible downgrade from BB.
Capex undershooting expectations in 2027, which Ashmore sees as little supported by evidence.
vol_and_positioning: VIX futures at 19.8%, up 0.6% on the week.

geopolitical: Netanyahu reportedly pressed Trump to strike Iran immediately after the US midterms, while Trump prefers to let negotiations run and Bessent urges more time for economic pressure.

Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei reportedly ordered an immediate response without geographical limitations to any attack. Qatari mediators held over 12 hours of talks in Tehran, and Iran has threatened oil and gas facilities in five Gulf states if struck.
Zelenskyy said Ukraine is ready to discuss territorial issues with Russia at leaders' level. Russia is ready to resume talks with the US and Ukraine after 4 November, possibly in Abu Dhabi.
Saudi Aramco and ADNOC are expanding export capacity that bypasses Hormuz.
Mexico's Economy Minister Ebrard acknowledged the US midterms are unlikely to bring lower tariffs on steel, aluminium and vehicles.

tension_points.bull_case: Ashmore sees little fundamental reason for the sell-off. Cloud revenue growth is accelerating (103% at Google, 48% at Microsoft, 39% at Amazon), 2027 capex is guided to rise significantly, and S&P IT at 18x forward earnings is below dotcom-bust lows.
tension_points.bear_case: Risk-off sentiment, financing concerns and hedge fund de-leveraging persist, the Fed is hiking with a December hike 75% priced, and even net-cash AI capex names have derated.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A significant undershoot of 2027 capex versus expectations, which Ashmore says there is little evidence of.

tension_points.bull_case: Other models that incorporate past results and poll biases suggest a good chance Republicans keep control of the Senate.
tension_points.bear_case: Prediction markets price a 73% chance of a Democratic Senate and 95% for the House, which could add negative AI sentiment given anti-data-centre rhetoric.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Republicans retaining the Senate would undercut the bear case on policy risk to AI.
